_readme: Adverse reputation flags that are already known, understood and accepted.
scripts/check-exit-reputation.py exits 1 on any adverse flag NOT listed here,
so adding an entry is a deliberate human decision and that is the point:
somebody has to look at a new flag once before it becomes background noise.
Keyed by node NAME, never by address -- this file is committed and this
Before accepting a flag, read docs/design/ban-safety.md. Accepting is for
flags that are a property of the range rather than of our traffic. A flag
that reflects what our own customers are doing is an incident, not a
Removing a node from the fleet? Delete its entry, or the next reviewer will
think a flag is still accepted when the node it belonged to is gone.

why.de1: ipapi.is:is_abuser -- LightNode / Kaopu Cloud (AS154177). A control address in the same /24, measured in docs/research/gaming-ip-reputation.md, carries the same flag, which points at the range rather than at our traffic. Accepted as a range property, NOT as harmless: docs/node-enumerability-remediation.md section 4 is the open action, and the first step there is re-checking that control. If the control ever comes back clean while de1 does not, this entry must be removed and treated as an incident.
why.tr1: ipapi.is:is_abuser -- same finding, same operator. Note the two feeds disagree on tr1's ASN: ipapi.is says AS154177 LIGHT NODE LIMITED, ip-api.com says AS2914 NTT America with org 'Light Node Limited' and hosting=false. Sub-allocated space. The hosting=false reading is the best ASN-type posture in the fleet.
why.fr1: proxycheck.io:proxy=yes type=VPN risk=66 -- a prefix verdict on Linode/Akamai (AS63949), not a behavioural one. The panel host, which has never carried a tunnel, measures identically on Hetzner; so does an unrelated neighbour address in each range. proxycheck is scoring the range. The four other feeds all read clean.
why.fi1: proxycheck.io:proxy=yes type=VPN risk=66 -- same, on Hetzner (AS24940).
why.sg1: proxycheck.io:proxy=yes type=VPN risk=66 -- same, on Linode/Akamai (AS63949).
